head: Title and extent of operation
gist: IPC applies to whole of India. Offences committed by Indian citizens outside India also covered.

head: Common intention
gist: When several persons act with common intention, each is liable as if the act were done by them alone.

head: Right of private defence
gist: Nothing is an offence done in exercise of the right of private defence — must be proportionate to threat.

head: When private defence extends to causing death
gist: Right to cause death in private defence arises only in 6 specific situations — assault with reasonable apprehension of death, etc.

head: Abetment
gist: Abetment = instigating, conspiring, or aiding commission of an offence. Abettor is punishable as if principal offender.

head: Criminal conspiracy
gist: Agreement between 2+ persons to do an illegal act or legal act by illegal means. Punishable even if the act is not carried out.

head: Sedition (stayed by SC 2022)
gist: Words/acts exciting disaffection towards Government. Currently stayed by Supreme Court pending review — no new FIRs without govt permission.

head: Culpable homicide
gist: Causing death with intention of causing death OR with knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.

head: Murder (when CulpHom = Murder)
gist: Culpable homicide is murder when done with intent to cause death; or with intent to cause such injury as is sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course.

head: Punishment for murder
gist: Death or imprisonment for life + fine.

head: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
gist: Part I (with intention): 10 yrs–life + fine. Part II (knowledge only): up to 10 yrs or fine or both.

head: Causing death by negligence
gist: Causing death by rash or negligent act not amounting to CulpHom. Up to 2 years or fine or both.

head: Abetment of suicide
gist: If a person commits suicide, the person who abetted it is punishable with up to 10 years + fine.

head: Rape
gist: Sexual act without consent or with consent obtained by fraud, force, or when unable to consent. Marital rape (wife over 18) not included.

head: Punishment for rape
gist: Minimum 10 years rigorous imprisonment, extendable to life. Death penalty possible in repeat offences or child rape.

head: Theft
gist: Dishonest taking of movable property from another's possession without consent. Up to 3 years + fine.

head: Extortion
gist: Intentionally putting a person in fear and delivering property/valuable security. Up to 3 years + fine.

head: Robbery
gist: Theft or extortion becomes robbery when attended by hurt, or threat of hurt, at the time. Up to 10 years + fine.

head: Criminal breach of trust
gist: Dishonest misappropriation of property entrusted. Up to 3 years or fine or both.

head: Cheating
gist: Fraudulently or dishonestly deceiving a person to deliver property or consent. Act or omission must cause damage/harm.

head: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
gist: Aggravated cheating — up to 7 years + fine.

head: Criminal trespass
gist: Entering property in possession of another with intent to commit offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy.

head: Forgery
gist: Making a false document or part of document with intent to cause damage, support a fraudulent claim, or commit fraud.

head: Defamation
gist: Imputation to harm reputation — by words, signs, or visible representations. Truth, public good, and fair comment are defences.

head: Criminal intimidation
gist: Threatening injury to a person, his reputation or property to cause alarm or compel them to do something.

head: When police may arrest without warrant
gist: Police can arrest without warrant only for cognizable offences. For non-cognizable, warrant or Magistrate order needed.

head: Notice to appear
gist: For offences punishable up to 7 years, police must first issue notice — cannot arrest immediately without Magistrate approval.

head: Right to know grounds of arrest
gist: Arrested person must be immediately informed of grounds of arrest and right to bail (if bailable).

head: Produced before Magistrate within 24 hours
gist: No person arrested shall be detained beyond 24 hours without a Magistrate's order — fundamental right (Art 22).

head: Maintenance of wives, children and parents
gist: Magistrate can order monthly maintenance. Wife includes divorced wife if not remarried. Neglect or refusal required.

head: First Information Report (FIR)
gist: Police must register FIR for cognizable offences — refusal is itself an offence. Can be sent by post to SP.

head: Examination of witnesses by police
gist: Police can orally examine any person acquainted with facts. Accused cannot be compelled to answer against himself (Art 20).

head: Recording of confessions and statements
gist: Magistrate must ensure confession is voluntary. 15-minute wait given. Confessions before police are NOT admissible.

head: Report of police officer on completion of investigation
gist: Final report (charge sheet if evidence sufficient, or closure report). Must be submitted within 60/90 days.

head: When accused shall be discharged
gist: Magistrate must discharge accused if no case made out against them after considering police report and accused's defence.

head: Power to examine the accused
gist: Court shall examine accused after prosecution evidence to explain incriminating circumstances — accused cannot be compelled.

head: Appeals from conviction
gist: Any person convicted by Sessions Court can appeal to High Court. Acquittal appeals by State go to High Court.

head: Revision
gist: High Court and Sessions Court have revisional powers — can call for records and examine legality, propriety of lower court orders.

head: Anticipatory bail
gist: Pre-arrest bail from Sessions Court or High Court. Applies when person has reason to apprehend arrest. Conditions can be imposed.

head: Inherent powers of High Court
gist: High Court can quash any proceeding to prevent abuse of process or to secure ends of justice — wide discretionary power.

head: Courts to try all civil suits
gist: Courts have jurisdiction to try all civil suits unless expressly or impliedly barred. Presumption of jurisdiction.

head: Res Judicata
gist: A matter directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between same parties shall not be tried again.

head: Other suits to be instituted where defendant resides
gist: Suits may be filed where defendant resides, carries on business, or where cause of action arises.

head: Notice to government before suit
gist: 2 months notice must be given before suing the Government or a Public Officer — failing which suit is not maintainable.

head: Appeal from original decree
gist: Every decree passed in original suit is appealable to Appellate Court. No second appeal on facts — only on substantial question of law.

head: Second appeal
gist: Second appeal lies to High Court only on substantial question of law — not on findings of fact.

head: Representative suits
gist: Where many persons have same interest, one or more may sue or be sued on behalf of all — class action.

head: Summary suits
gist: Summary procedure for recovery of money based on bills of exchange, hundis, promissory notes — defendant must apply for leave to defend.

head: Temporary injunctions
gist: Court may grant TI to restrain defendant from doing a prejudicial act. Three conditions: prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable harm.

head: Definitions — Facts, evidence, proved
gist: Fact: anything perceptible by senses or state of mind. Evidence: oral or documentary. Proved = beyond reasonable doubt (criminal), preponderance (civil).

head: Admission defined
gist: An admission is a statement suggesting an inference as to fact in issue or relevant fact — made by a party or their agent.

head: Confession caused by inducement — irrelevant
gist: Confession made due to threat, inducement or promise by a person in authority is irrelevant. Voluntariness is essential.

head: Discovery statement
gist: When fact discovered as consequence of information given by accused in custody, so much of information as relates to the fact discovered is admissible.

head: Opinion of experts
gist: When opinion on foreign law, science, art, handwriting, or finger impressions is relevant — opinion of expert is admissible.

head: Oral evidence must be direct
gist: Oral evidence in all cases must be direct — hearsay not admissible. Direct = perceived by witness personally.

head: Admissibility of electronic records
gist: Electronic records admissible only with 65B certificate from person responsible for device. Certificate confirms authenticity.

head: Burden of proof
gist: Whoever desires any court to give judgment as to right or liability must prove the facts. He who asserts must prove.

head: Presumption as to abetment of suicide by married woman
gist: If suicide within 7 years of marriage and husband/relatives committed cruelty — court may presume abetment.

head: Presumption as to absence of consent in rape
gist: If victim states she did not consent, court SHALL presume she did not consent. Burden shifts to accused.

head: Proposal (Offer)
gist: When one person signifies to another willingness to do/abstain from doing something with a view to obtaining assent.

head: Acceptance
gist: When person to whom proposal is made signifies assent to it — becomes a promise.

head: Contract
gist: An agreement enforceable by law. Agreement = promise or set of promises forming consideration for each other.

head: What agreements are contracts
gist: Agreements are contracts if made by free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration, and lawful object.

head: Who is competent to contract
gist: Competent = major (18+) + sound mind + not disqualified by law. Minor's contract is void ab initio.

head: Consent
gist: Two or more persons are said to consent when they agree upon the same thing in the same sense (consensus ad idem).

head: Free consent
gist: Consent free when not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, or mistake.

head: Unlawful consideration and object
gist: Consideration/object unlawful if forbidden by law, fraudulent, involves injury to person/property, or against public policy.

head: Agreement without consideration is void
gist: No consideration = no contract (generally). Exceptions: love and affection, past voluntary service, time-barred debt.

head: Obligation to perform promise
gist: Parties to a contract must either perform or offer to perform their respective promises unless performance dispensed with.

head: Agreement to do impossible act — void
gist: Agreement to do impossible act is void. If act becomes impossible after contract, contract becomes void (frustrated contract).

head: Liability to return advantage received under coercion or mistake
gist: Money paid or thing delivered under coercion/mistake must be repaid or returned.

head: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach
gist: Party who suffers from breach entitled to receive compensation for loss naturally arising — remoteness of damage rule.

head: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated
gist: Whether reasonable compensation or penalty, court awards only reasonable compensation not exceeding penalty amount.

head: Definition of State
gist: 'State' includes the Government and Parliament of India, Government and Legislature of each State, all local authorities, and other authorities within India.

head: Laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void
gist: Pre-Constitutional laws inconsistent with FRs void to extent of inconsistency. State cannot make law taking away or abridging FRs.

head: Equality before law
gist: The State shall not deny to any person equality before law or equal protection of laws. Reasonable classification permitted.

head: Equality of opportunity in public employment
gist: Equal opportunity in matters of public employment. No discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence.

head: Abolition of untouchability
gist: Untouchability abolished and its practice in any form forbidden. Enforcement is punishable as offence.

head: Protection of six freedoms
gist: (1)(a) Speech & expression (b) Assemble peacefully (c) Form associations (d) Move freely (e) Reside/settle (g) Practise any profession.

head: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
gist: No ex post facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination — these rights cannot be suspended even during Emergency.

head: Protection of life and personal liberty
gist: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Widest interpretation by SC.

head: Right to education
gist: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6–14 years. Added by 86th Amendment 2002.

head: Protection against arrest and detention
gist: Right to be informed of grounds of arrest, consult lawyer, produced before Magistrate within 24 hours. Preventive detention has separate rules.

head: Freedom of conscience and free profession of religion
gist: Right to freely profess, practise and propagate religion — subject to public order, morality, health, and other FRs.

head: Remedies for enforcement of fundamental rights
gist: Right to move Supreme Court for enforcement of FRs. Court can issue writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, certiorari, prohibition, quo warranto.

head: Uniform Civil Code (DPSP)
gist: State shall endeavour to secure for citizens a Uniform Civil Code. Directive Principle — not enforceable. Goa has a common civil code.

head: Fundamental Duties
gist: 11 Fundamental Duties — added by 42nd Amendment 1976, 11th by 86th Amendment 2002. Not enforceable but used in interpretation.

head: Establishment of Supreme Court
gist: SC consists of CJI + not more than 33 other judges. Appointed by President after consultation (now collegium system).

head: Special leave to appeal by Supreme Court
gist: SC may in its discretion grant SLP from any judgment of any court or tribunal — discretionary, not an appeal as of right.

head: Power of High Courts to issue writs
gist: HC can issue writs for enforcement of FRs AND any other purpose — wider than Art 32 which is limited to FRs only.

head: Right to property
gist: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law. Constitutional right (not FR since 44th Amendment 1978).
